hero.body: Two tracks, six stages, a library of short lessons and code labs that run in the browser. No shortcuts — only foundations.

roadmap.title: Two tracks, six stages, one destination.
roadmap.body: You don't need to code to begin. The Applied track is for professionals in other fields; the Technical track is for engineers and researchers. Both share one conceptual vocabulary, so you can switch lanes at any point.

tracks.name: Applied track
tracks.blurb: For content, business, operations and management people — understand AI deeply enough to use it and decide well.

stages.title: How AI actually works
stages.body: How models learn from data, why they fail, and where the real limits sit.

stages.title: AI in your work
stages.body: Prompt design, workflows with a model inside, and measurement instead of vibes.

stages.title: Leading an organisation
stages.body: Weighing risk, data and cost; choosing what to automate and what to leave alone.

tracks.name: Technical track
tracks.blurb: For engineers, students and researchers — write code, train models, ship them, and read the literature.

stages.title: Data foundations & Python
stages.body: Linear algebra, probability and data wrangling, learned in live notebooks.

stages.title: Machine & deep learning
stages.body: From regression to transformers: implement, train and debug them yourself.

stages.title: LLMs, RAG & agents
stages.body: Fine-tuning, retrieval, multi-step agents, and getting them into production.

items.title: Artificial intelligence, explained from scratch
items.body: Six short lessons that assemble the whole picture: data, models, training, inference.

items.title: Deep learning with PyTorch
items.body: Reimplement each layer, train on shared GPUs, and compare against real baselines.

items.title: Building enterprise RAG systems
items.body: From internal documents to cited answers: chunking, embedding, retrieval, evaluation.

items.title: Multi-step agents and tools
items.body: Planning, tool calls, self-verification — and how to keep an agent on the rails.

journal.title: Essays from our content team.
journal.body: One short analysis each week: a single concept opened down to its mechanism, with runnable examples.

posts.title: Why a model stays confident while being wrong
posts.body: Rereading hallucination through the probability mechanics of token sampling, with a small experiment you can rerun.

posts.title: Reading AI papers without drowning
posts.body: A seven-step order for opening a deep learning paper: from the architecture figure to the experiments — and the parts everyone skips.

posts.title: Text embeddings: what the textbooks leave out
posts.body: Where embedding space distorts, why cosine similarity misleads, and what to measure instead.

closing.title: Begin at the first stage, today.
closing.body: Preview the whole roadmap, take the first three lessons of any stage, and decide only once you know where you are headed.
